# 187_Adjuvant_and_Neoadjuvant_Therapy_for_Colorectal_Cancer_Molecular-Based_Therapy_Including_Landmark_Trials.qmd








```{r}
#| label: evolution of CRC trials

library(ggplot2)

library(dplyr)

trials <- tibble::tribble(

~year, ~trial, ~group,

2019, "CAO/ARO/AIO-12", "LARC",

2019, "Polish II", "LARC",

2021, "PRODIGE 23", "LARC",

2021, "RAPIDO", "LARC",

2022, "DYNAMIC", "Colon",

2022, "STELLAR", "LARC",

2022, "OPRA", "LARC",

2022, "dMMR rectal cancer PD-1", "Immunotherapy",

2023, "FOxTROT", "Colon",

2023, "OPERA", "Early rectal",

2023, "NEO", "Early rectal",

2021, "TREC", "Early rectal"

)

ggplot(trials, aes(x = year, y = reorder(trial, year), color = group)) +

geom_point(size = 3) +

geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "grey70") +

theme_minimal() +

labs(x = "Year", y = "Trial", title = "Evolution of colorectal cancer trials")
```

### Rectal cancer neoadjuvant/TNT trials

- Polish II: SCRT + consolidation FOLFOX vs standard LCCRT in fixed cT3/cT4 disease.
- PRODIGE 23: induction FOLFIRINOX → LCCRT → TME → adjuvant therapy vs standard LCCRT → TME → adjuvant therapy.
- RAPIDO: SCRT → consolidation CAPOX/FOLFOX → TME vs LCCRT → TME ± adjuvant chemotherapy for high-risk LARC. 
- STELLAR: SCRT → CAPOX → TME → adjuvant CAPOX vs LCCRT → TME → adjuvant CAPOX.
- OPRA/CAO-ARO-AIO-12: compare induction chemotherapy before CRT vs CRT before consolidation chemotherapy, relevant to organ preservation.

### Colon cancer neoadjuvant trial

- FOxTROT: neoadjuvant + adjuvant FOLFOX vs adjuvant-only FOLFOX in operable locally advanced colon cancer. [8]

### Key adjuvant trials in colorectal cancer

- Early adjuvant colon cancer trials established that 5-FU–based therapy improved survival in stage III colon cancer. This laid the foundation for postoperative chemotherapy as standard treatment. 
- The MOSAIC trial showed that adding oxaliplatin to 5-FU/LV improved disease-free survival, establishing 6 months of adjuvant FOLFOX as the standard for stage III colon cancer. 
- Later trials showed CAPOX and FOLFOX were equivalent as adjuvant options, giving flexibility in regimen choice. 
- The IDEA collaboration compared 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant therapy in stage III colon cancer. 3 months of CAPOX was noninferior for most patients; 3 months of FOLFOX was reasonable for low-risk patients, but high-risk patients benefited more from 6 months of FOLFOX. Shorter treatment also had better tolerance. 
- In stage II colon cancer, benefit is smaller, so adjuvant treatment is mainly considered for high-risk features.
